title: A Study on Antibiotic Pattern of Urinary Tract Infections Causing Gram Negative Bacteria
author: Chittineni Krishna Prasad
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Collect and transport urine sample
steps.instruction: Obtain a midstream urine (MSU) sample from each patient aged > 18 years, label it properly, place it in a self‑sealing polythene cover with two compartments (requisition form in one compartment, sample in the other) and transport the sample to the laboratory immediately.

steps.title: Inoculate urine onto agar plates
steps.instruction: Using the collected MSU sample, inoculate three separate agar plates: Cysteine‑lactose‑electrolyte‑deficient (CLED) agar, MacConkey agar, and blood agar.

substeps.instruction: Streak the urine onto a CLED agar plate.
Streak the urine onto a MacConkey agar plate.
Streak the urine onto a blood agar plate.

steps.title: Incubate plates at 37°C
steps.instruction: Place the inoculated CLED, MacConkey, and blood agar plates in an incubator set to 37 °C and incubate for 48 hours.

steps.title: Identify bacterial growth
steps.instruction: After incubation, examine the plates and identify any bacterial growth according to the laboratory’s standard identification protocol.

steps.title: Perform Kirby‑Bauer susceptibility test
steps.instruction: Carry out antimicrobial susceptibility testing on the isolated Gram‑negative bacteria using the Kirby‑Bauer disc diffusion method on Mueller‑Hinton agar medium.
